stem: Which parent statement demonstrates correct understanding of safe sleep positioning for a newborn?

options.A: I will place my baby on the back for every sleep on a firm, flat, noninclined sleep surface
options.B: Side sleeping is safer than back sleeping because spit-up can drain from the mouth
options.C: Prone sleeping is recommended for routine nighttime sleep if I am in the same room
options.D: An inclined sleeper is appropriate if the baby has uncomplicated reflux

rationale: AAP safe-sleep guidance recommends placing infants supine for every sleep on a firm, flat, noninclined surface. Side sleeping is not recommended, routine prone sleep increases sleep-related death risk, and inclined sleep surfaces are unsafe; uncomplicated reflux is not an indication to abandon supine sleep. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Teach caregivers to place infants on the back for every sleep on a firm, flat, noninclined surface.
source_document_title: Sleep-Related Infant Deaths: Updated 2022 Recommendations for Reducing Infant Deaths in the Sleep Environment; Safe Sleep: 9 Ways to Reduce a Baby's Risk of SIDS & Suffocation
source_version_date: AAP policy remains current; HealthyChildren safe-sleep content updated 2026; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: AAP recommendations: 'Back to sleep for every sleep' and 'Use a firm, flat, noninclined sleep surface'; HealthyChildren 2026 safe-sleep guidance repeats back positioning for naps/nighttime and firm noninclined sleep surface
source_claim_supported: Infants should be placed supine for every sleep on a firm, flat, noninclined surface; side/prone routine positioning and inclined sleepers are not recommended.

correction_summary: Converted the definition-style item into parent-teaching validation and added realistic unsafe alternatives involving side sleep, prone sleep, and reflux-related inclination without expanding beyond the safe-sleep construct.
audit_findings: A is the direct AAP recommendation. B, C and D conflict with current safe-sleep guidance. No second defensible answer, cueing, or unsupported duration/monitoring rule remains. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
